correctness.rationale: For a partial injection, f squared is empty if and only if domain and image are disjoint. Graph distances within and across the nonempty parts are precisely 2 and 1, making the image part assignment injective. Every such part injection yields exactly the independent binomial/factorial choices counted; the image part assignment is uniquely recovered, so there is no overcount. The bipartite count separates the preserving and exchanging patterns with one empty-map correction. Their capacity constraints give exact rank maxima and the parity defect, and restriction yields every lower rank. Independently, exhaustive direct distance tests matched all coefficients for 19 graphs (6,119 accepted maps in aggregate).

value.rationale: The square-zero element-rank polynomial is a natural invariant of an inverse transformation monoid. It is determined in every degree for the entire complete multipartite graph family, beyond isolated small numerics; the exact capacity and parity obstruction for bipartite graphs identifies a genuinely structural boundary. K3,5 and K4,4 share eight vertices but have maximal square-zero ranks three and four, respectively, showing that the count detects the graph partition structure and is not recoverable from vertex number alone. The value claim is the full family classification, not an individual trivial complete-graph or C4 specialization.
